messages.subject: Ffilter - wav with lower quality
parts:
Hello,

Dorian Gravier, I am a student working on bats in Konstanz (Germany).

I am actually looking to find automaticly feeding buzzes of bats. For this I am using the amplitude function of the time and check different parameters with an other software. The problem is that I have some noise in some sequences below 20 or 25KHz. My goal is to filter sequences between 20 KHz and 100 for example.

I try the function ffilter() it seems to work but the quality (maybe I can define this as decibels) of the resulting wave is less than the other. I join 2 waves, before and after the function.

I used this code : savewav(ffilter(readWave('Before.wav'),from=20000,to=100000,f=500000),filename=After.wav',f=500000)

My goal is to have exactly the same file without frequencies between from and to.

I had also this problem to change the sampling rate. But it works by using repw(), Wave() and writeWave().

I tried with those functions but without success. Can you help me in this ?

My second goal will be to batch this, but I will try this if a solution appears to my problems.
Thx for your help.
Regards.

>
> My goal is to have exactly the same file without frequencies between from

Yes ffilter() is based on an inverse FFT and might slightly impair
the sound. You should use the function fir() instead which is faster
and does not change the sound at all.

>
> I had also this problem to change the sampling rate. But it works by using
> repw(), Wave() and writeWave().
>
> I tried with those functions but without success. Can you help me in this ?

I am not sure to understand what you mean. Can you please specify or
give some code?

Best regards

Jerome

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Ffilter - wav with lower quality
parts:
Hi,

I took a look to what you told me.

I succeed, thank you so much. I used this fonction :

writeWave(fir(readWave('Before.wav'),from=20000,f=500000,output="Wave"),filename='After_Fir_writeWave.wav')

This delete the noise between 0 and 20kHz. But it is much slower than with ffilter().

The thing with savewav() is that in this latter code, if I use savewav() instead of writeWave() the quality of the sound is worse.
So I have one question ? savewav() is it also done for saving a R object that is already a wave ?

Concerning what I told you, my goal was to pass a wave in "time expansion" (x per 10 the time). My idea was to use first as Jean-François Julien (I guess you know him) told me, to use resamp() because usually (in Batsound software for example) we just have to divide the sampling rate per 10.
But it does not work because the function is not exactly done for what I wanted (it is a resampling). For your information, Jean-François made a script and it works. I join it. Maybe it could be possible in the future to create a function for doing what the script does (idea).

In this script, the code could be synthesize like this : writeWave(Wave(left=repw(readWave("Before.wav",f=500000),times=1,ouput="matrix"),samp.rate=50000,bit=16),file="After.wav")
I used savewav() instead of writeWave(), the result is the same, the quality is worse. So I am just wondering that it is explained by the fact of savewav() use already writeWave() (but also in the last code, Wave()).

I hope I am clear in my explanations.

Regards
Dorian.

Ps : I have an other question but I will create a new subject.

2012/5/4 Jérôme SUEUR <su...@mnhn.fr>
